best_for: Owners of a Ledger hardware wallet who want to check balances, send coins and approve each transaction on the device from a desktop computer.
description:
Ledger Wallet, formerly Ledger Live, is the companion app that Ledger makes for its hardware signers. There is no account, email or password to set up. You get in with your Ledger device and its PIN, and Ledger never holds your coins.

Through the app you install coin apps on your device, update its firmware, and check a receiving address on the device screen before you share it. Clear Signing shows the full details of a transaction on the device, so you can read what you are approving. The portfolio view shows live market data. When you buy, the app compares quotes from more than 50 providers.

points.title: Now called Ledger Wallet
points.text: Ledger renamed Ledger Live to Ledger Wallet. It is the same desktop and mobile app, so older guides that say Ledger Live still apply.

points.title: Made for Ledger hardware
points.text: Your private keys live on a Ledger device, and every transaction must be approved on it. Without the hardware the app is of little use, so it is not a general software wallet.

points.title: Wide coin coverage
points.text: Ledger lists support for over 15,000 coins and tokens across more than 100 blockchains, with a portfolio view and send and receive built in. It also connects to decentralized apps without a browser extension.

points.title: Buy, swap and stake go through partners
points.text: The app itself is free with no subscription. Buying, selling and swapping run through third-party providers that charge their own fees, and network fees still apply. Ledger takes no staking fee, but validators may take a cut, and rewards are not guaranteed.

points.title: Signed updates
points.text: Ledger signs its desktop releases, and the built-in updater checks the signature before it applies an update. For a first install, take the download from Ledger's own site rather than a link someone sent you.

points.title: Platform notes
points.text: The macOS build is universal and needs macOS 13 or later. Ledger also makes a Linux build, which needs USB libraries to talk to the device, but this site lists only Windows and macOS.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 90 versions of the machine-wide installer. macOS lists only the current release, so a downgrade there needs another source.
